sections.name: test_sync_parses_bundled_starter_template
sections.title: Running the sync on the starter template
sections.what: Copies the starter guidelines and tokens into a temporary folder, runs the sync there, and checks for crashes. It then confirms the primary, secondary, and accent 500 shades match the expected codes. It skips when Node is not installed.
sections.why: Runs the real script against the starter template, which catches the crash without touching project files.
sections.watch_out: The expected codes are written into the test, so any change to the starter colors needs the test updated too.

summary: An automated test that runs the brand sync on the bundled starter template and checks that it finishes and writes the expected primary, secondary, and accent colors.
purpose: Catches a past crash so the sync cannot fail on its own starter template again without anyone noticing.
why: Records a real bug: the color parser used to fail on the starter layout and crash with a type error. The header says the test runs under the existing pytest checks.
how: The test copies the starter guidelines and starter token file into a temporary folder, runs the sync script there with Node, checks that no type error appears and the exit code is zero, then reads the token file and compares three shade values to expected hex codes.
inputs: The starter guidelines template, the starter token template, and the sync script.
outputs: A pass or fail result for pytest. It writes only into a temporary folder.
risks: The expected color codes are fixed in the test, so changing the starter colors makes the test fail even if the script is fine.
debug: Run the test alone with pytest. If it skips, Node is not installed. If it fails on a type error, look at the parser for the color sections. If it fails on a color value, compare the starter template with the expected codes.
